blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 1

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.

The Blockbuster Phenomenon: A New Museum Trend

Museums in Australia, like other pleasure-giving public organizations, are adapting their activities so that they more closely reflect the marketplace.

A Since the 1980s, the term ‘blockbuster' has become the fashionable word for spectacular, high-profile museum exhibitions that have the ability to attract large crowds. A blockbuster is a 'large-scale loan exhibition that people who normally don't go to museums will stand in line for hours to see' (Eisen 1984). Once the museum that created the exhibition has shown it to its local market, it can be offered to other organizations for a fee. This means that you can boost your own door takings and make money from boosting someone else's door takings.

B While partaking of the excitement of the blockbuster, visitors thus lured are likely to stay longer at the museum. Betty Churcher, when Director of the Australian National Gallery, summed up the new blockbuster creed as follows: 'The bonus of the blockbuster exhibitions is that people come to see the blockbuster and they stay to look at the permanent collection, so you are getting broader exposure for your collection.'

C Museums across the UK, USA, Canada and Australia currently operate under a system of plural funding: revenue raised through contributions by federal, state and/or local governments, combined with revenue raised through admission charges and other activities. Maintaining and increasing visitor levels is thus paramount and involves not only creating or hiring blockbuster exhibitions, but providing regular exhibition changes and innovations. In addition, the visiting public have become known as customers rather than visitors, and the skills that are valued in museums to keep the new customers coming through the door have changed. Curators are now administrators, and being a museum director no longer requires an Arts degree—but public relations skills are essential if the museum is going to compete with other museums to stage travelling exhibitions which draw huge crowds.

D The convergence of museums, the heritage industry, tourism, profit-making and pleasure-giving has resulted in the new 'museology'. This has given rise to much debate about whether it is appropriate to see museums primarily as tourist attractions. In literature from both the UK and USA, the words that are starting to appear in some descriptions of blockbusters are ‘less scholarly', 'non-elitist' and 'popularist', while others extol the virtues of encouraging scholars to co-operate on projects, and to provide exhibitions that cater for a broad selection of the community rather than an elite sector. Whatever commentators may think, managers of museums worldwide are looking for artful ways to blend culture and commerce, and blockbuster exhibitions are at the top of the list.

E But do blockbusters held in public institutions really create a surplus to fund other activities? If the bottom line is profit, then according to the records of many major museums blockbusters do make money. For museums in some countries, it may be the money that they require to replace parts of their collections or to fix buildings that are in need of attention. For some museums in Australia, it may be the opportunity to illustrate that they are attempting to pay their way by recovering part of their operating costs. Also, creating or hiring a blockbuster has many positive spin-offs: blockbusters mean crowds, and crowds are good for the local economy, providing increased trade for shops, hotels, restaurants, the transport industry and retailers. The argument that the arts provide sustained economic benefits has been well illustrated in impact studies in the USA and UK.

F However, blockbusters require large capital expenditure and draw on resources across all branches of an organization, and the costs don't end there. There is a Human Resource Management cost in addition to a measurable 'real' dollar cost. Receiving a touring exhibition draws resources from across functional management structures in a project-management style. Everyone—from general labourers to building services, front-of-house, technical, promotional, educational and administrative staff—is required to perform additional tasks. Furthermore, as an increasing number of institutions try their hand at increasing visitor numbers and memberships (and therefore revenue) by staging blockbuster exhibitions, it may be less likely that blockbusters will continue to provide a surplus to subsidize other activities due to the competitive nature of the market.

G It has been illustrated in both the UK and USA that the blockbuster ideology has resulted in the false expectation that the momentum required to stage blockbusters can be maintained continually. Creating, mounting or hiring blockbusters is exhausting, with the real costs throughout an institution difficult to calculate. Secondly, as some analysts have argued, the 'shopkeeping' mentality and cost-benefit analysis, and a pure concentration on the bottom line, can squeeze substance out of an exhibition. Taking out substance can be a recipe for blockbuster failure and therefore financial failure.

H Perhaps the best pathway to take is one that balances both blockbusters and regular exhibitions. However, this easy middle ground may only work if you have enough space, and have alternative sources of funding to continue to support the regular, less exciting fare. Perhaps the advice should be to make sure that you find out what your local community wants from you and make sure that your regular activities and exhibitions are more enduring.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 1–4

Reading Passage 1 has eight paragraphs, A–H.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

Write the correct letter, A–H, in boxes 1–4 on your answer sheet.

NB You may use any letter more than once.

ABCDEFGH
1 the reason why museum directors need to constantly alter and update their exhibits
2 mention of the length of time people will queue to see a blockbuster
3 terms that people have used when referring to blockbusters
4 the various ways that institutions like museums get financial support

Questions 5–8

Complete the sentences below.

Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.

5 These days, museum visitors tend to be referred to as .
6 Museum curators now need rather than academic qualifications.
7 The linking of a range of public institutions that entertain the public is known as .
8 There is discussion about whether museums can be regarded in the same way as other .

Questions 9 and 10

Choose TWO letters, A–E.

Which TWO of the following are mentioned by the writer as advantages of blockbusters?

Questions 11–13

Choose THREE letters, A–G.

Which THREE of the following are mentioned by the writer as disadvantages of blockbusters?

meta.matchedTitle: The Blockbuster Phenomenon 博物馆爆款现象

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 20 世纪 80 年代起，“爆款展览（blockbuster）” 成为博物馆大型高关注度展览的流行术语，指 “能吸引平时不逛博物馆的人排队数小时观看的大型外借展览”（Eisen 1984）。举办方在本地展出后，可将展览有偿提供给其他机构，既能提升自身门票收入，也能通过助力其他机构盈利。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 观众被爆款展览吸引后，通常会在博物馆停留更久。澳大利亚国家美术馆前馆长贝蒂・丘彻（Betty Churcher）总结爆款展览的价值：“爆款展览的额外收获是，观众为看爆款而来，却会留下来参观常设藏品，从而让馆内藏品获得更广泛的关注。”

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 英、美、加、澳的博物馆目前采用 “多元资助体系”：资金来自联邦、州或地方政府资助，以及门票收入和其他活动收益。因此，维持并提升观众数量至关重要，措施包括打造或引进爆款展览、定期更换展览并创新。此外，观众被称为 “顾客（customers）” 而非 “访客（visitors）”，博物馆所需技能也发生变化：策展人需兼任管理者，馆长无需艺术学位，但需具备公关技能以与其他博物馆竞争举办吸引大量观众的巡回展览。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 博物馆、遗产产业、旅游业、盈利与娱乐机构的融合催生了新 “博物馆学（museology）”，引发关于 “博物馆是否应首要视为旅游景点” 的争议。英美文献中，描述爆款展览的词汇逐渐出现 “学术性较弱（less scholarly）”“非精英化（non-elitist）”“大众化（popularist）”，也有观点称赞其 “鼓励学者合作、满足广泛群体而非精英阶层需求”。无论评论如何，全球博物馆管理者都在寻找融合文化与商业的巧妙方式，而爆款展览是首要选择。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 公共机构举办的爆款展览是否真能创造盈余以资助其他活动？若以盈利为目标，多数大型博物馆记录显示爆款展览确实赚钱：部分国家的博物馆用这笔钱更新藏品或维修建筑；澳大利亚部分博物馆则借此收回部分运营成本。此外，爆款展览还带来诸多间接益处：吸引大量观众，带动当地经济，提升商店、酒店、餐厅、交通和零售业的营业额。美国和英国的影响研究已充分证明艺术产业能带来持续经济收益。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 然而，爆款展览需大量资本投入，且占用机构各部门资源，成本不止于此：除可量化的资金成本外，还涉及人力资源成本。引进巡回展览需各职能部门以项目管理模式投入资源，从普通劳工到建筑服务、前台、技术、宣传、教育和行政人员，均需承担额外工作。此外，随着越来越多机构通过举办爆款展览提升观众量和会员数（进而增加收入），市场竞争加剧，爆款展览能否持续创造盈余补贴其他活动，可能性正逐渐降低。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 英美案例显示，爆款理念引发 “可持续举办爆款展览” 的错误预期。打造、举办或引进爆款展览耗费精力，机构内部的实际成本难以计算。其次，正如部分分析师所言，“店铺经营思维”“成本效益分析” 和 “单纯关注盈利” 可能会削弱展览的实质内容，而内容缺失可能导致爆款展览失败，进而引发财务亏损。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph H
passageNotes.text: 或许最佳路径是平衡爆款展览与常规展览，但这一折中方案需满足两个条件：足够的空间，以及用于支持常规（吸引力较低）展览的其他资金来源。或许更合理的建议是：了解当地社区需求，确保常规活动与展览更具持久性。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 1. 段落匹配（Questions 1–4：Which paragraph contains the following information?）

items.text:
（1）题目 1：the reason why museum directors need to constantly alter and update their exhibits
题目翻译：博物馆馆长需要不断更改和更新展品的原因
答案：C
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “Maintaining and increasing visitor levels is thus paramount and involves not only creating or hiring blockbuster exhibitions, but providing regular exhibition changes and innovations”，明确指出 “为维持并提升观众数量”，馆长需定期更换展览，即 “不断更改和更新展品的原因”，与题干对应，因此答案为 C。

（2）题目 2：mention of the length of time people will queue to see a blockbuster
题目翻译：提及人们为看爆款展览会排队的时长
答案：A
解析：定位 Paragraph A 中 “A blockbuster is a ‘large-scale loan exhibition that people who normally don’t go to museums will stand in line for hours to see’ (Eisen 1984)”，明确提到人们会 “排队数小时（stand in line for hours）”，即 “排队时长”，与题干对应，因此答案为 A。

（3）题目 3：terms that people have used when referring to blockbusters
题目翻译：人们描述爆款展览时使用的术语
答案：D
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “the words that are starting to appear in some descriptions of blockbusters are ‘less scholarly’, ‘non-elitist’ and ‘popularist’”，明确列举了描述爆款展览的术语（学术性较弱、非精英化、大众化），与题干对应，因此答案为 D。

（4）题目 4：the various ways that institutions like museums get financial support
题目翻译：博物馆等机构获得财政支持的多种方式
答案：C
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “Museums across the UK, USA, Canada and Australia currently operate under a system of plural funding: revenue raised through contributions by federal, state and/or local governments, combined with revenue raised through admission charges and other activities”，明确列出资金来源（政府资助、门票收入、其他活动收益），即 “多种财政支持方式”，与题干对应，因此答案为 C。

questionExplanations.sectionTitle: 2. 句子填空（Questions 5–8：NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS）

items.text:
（1）题目 5：These days, museum visitors tend to be referred to as \___\___\___\_.
题目翻译：如今，博物馆观众往往被称为_\___\___\___。
答案：customers（顾客）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “the visiting public have become known as customers rather than visitors”，“become known as” 对应 “tend to be referred to as”，明确提到观众被称为 “顾客”，因此答案为 “customers”。

（2）题目 6：Museum curators now need \___\___\____ rather than academic qualifications.
题目翻译：如今博物馆策展人需要_\___\___\___，而非学术资格。
答案：public relations skills（公关技能）
解析：定位 Paragraph C 中 “Curators are now administrators, and being a museum director no longer requires an Arts degree-but public relations skills are essential”，“essential” 对应 “need”，明确提到策展人（延伸至馆长）需具备 “公关技能”，而非学术学位，因此答案为 “public relations skills”。

（3）题目 7：The linking of a range of public institutions that entertain the public is known as \___\___\___\_.
题目翻译：将一系列公共娱乐机构关联起来的概念被称为_\___\___\___。
答案：museology（博物馆学）
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “The convergence of museums, the heritage industry, tourism, profit-making and pleasure-giving has resulted in the new ‘museology’”，“convergence” 对应 “linking”，“public institutions that entertain the public” 对应 “museums, the heritage industry, tourism...”，明确提到这种融合产生的概念是 “博物馆学”，因此答案为 “museology”。

（4）题目 8：There is discussion about whether museums can be regarded in the same way as other \___\___\___\_.
题目翻译：关于博物馆是否能与其他_\___\___\___被同等看待，存在争议。
答案：tourist attractions（旅游景点）
解析：定位 Paragraph D 中 “this has given rise to much debate about whether it is appropriate to see museums primarily as tourist attractions”，“debate” 对应 “discussion”，“see... as” 对应 “be regarded in the same way as”，明确提到争议核心是博物馆是否能被视为 “旅游景点”，因此答案为 “tourist attractions”。

题目：Which TWO of the following are mentioned by the writer as advantages of blockbusters?（作者提到的爆款展览的两个优势是？）
答案：A、C
选项 A：Some of the money they raise can be used for structural repairs.（部分收益可用于建筑维修）
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “it may be the money they require to replace parts of their collections or to fix buildings that are in need of attention”，“fix buildings” 对应 “structural repairs”，明确提到收益可用于建筑维修，A 为优势。
- 选项 C：Local services benefit from the extra business they bring about.（当地服务业从其带来的额外业务中受益）
解析：定位 Paragraph E 中 “blockbusters mean crowds, and crowds are good for the local economy, providing increased trade for shops, hotels, restaurants, the transport industry and retailers”，“shops, hotels...” 对应 “local services”，明确提到当地服务业受益，C 为优势。
- 排除 B：文中未提及 “资助业余艺术家”；排除 D：未提及 “吸引海外劳工”；排除 E：未提及 “提升员工绩效”。

题目：Which THREE of the following are mentioned by the writer as disadvantages of blockbusters?（作者提到的爆款展览的三个劣势是？）
答案：C、E、G
选项 C：They involve an increased workload for personnel.（增加员工工作量）
解析：定位 Paragraph F 中 “Everyone-from general labourers to... administrative staff-is required to perform additional tasks”，“additional tasks” 对应 “increased workload”，明确提到员工需承担额外工作，C 为劣势。
- 选项 E：They are very tiring to put on.（举办起来非常耗费精力）
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “Creating, mounting or hiring blockbusters is exhausting”，“exhausting” 对应 “very tiring”，明确提到举办爆款展览耗费精力，E 为劣势。
- 选项 G：The content can be weakened through financial pressure.（内容可能因财务压力被削弱）
解析：定位 Paragraph G 中 “the ‘shopkeeping’ mentality and cost-benefit analysis, and a pure concentration on the bottom line, can squeeze substance out of an exhibition”，“squeeze substance out” 对应 “content can be weakened”，明确提到财务压力削弱展览内容，G 为劣势。
- 排除 A：文中提到需 “项目管理模式”，未说 “不适合管理风格”；排除 B：未提及 “支付专业商业咨询费用”；排除 D：未提及 “不提升年度观众总数”；排除 F：未提及 “跨国流行度差异”。
